item.text:
**Assessment**
- **Mixed, leaning negative.** 2024 shows broad macro gains and some inclusive public-service improvements, but the strongest subgroup-specific evidence points to persistent patronage, unequal treatment of Papuans, and policy capture that favored regime-linked networks rather than neutral distribution.

**Positive**
- [Macro Poverty Outlook for Indonesia: October 2024 Datasheet](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099026110152411280) — World Bank — 2024-10-02 — Poverty fell from 17.5% in 2023 to 15.8% in 2024, which is the clearest broad sign that gains were reaching ordinary households rather than only elite supporters. IDs: `5B.8`, `5B.6`.
- [Indonesia’s Climate Ambitions Gain Boost through World Bank-Supported Land Administration and Spatial Planning Reform](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/09/30/indonesia-s-climate-ambitions-gain-boost-through-world-bank-supported-land-administration-and-spatial-planning-reform) — World Bank — 2024-09-30 — The reform package was designed to strengthen tenure security, simplify licensing, reduce disputes, and improve productive investment, which supports a more even distribution of gains across regions and small landholders. IDs: `5B.8`, `5B.6`.
- [Indonesia](https://www.who.int/about/accountability/results/who-results-report-2024-2025/country-profile/2024/indonesia) — WHO — 2024 — WHO’s country profile credits Indonesia with 90% coverage, lower out-of-pocket costs, and better access to essential services irrespective of gender, age, or disability status. IDs: `5B.8`, `5B.6`.
- [Indonesia ramps up capacities to detect and respond to outbreaks of emerging and epidemic-prone diseases](https://www.who.int/indonesia/news/detail/30-08-2024-indonesia-ramps-up-capacities-to-detect-and-respond-to-outbreaks-of-emerging-and-epidemic-prone-diseases) — WHO Indonesia — 2024-08-30 — Rapid-response teams in 514 districts strengthened detection and response capacity across the country, which is a broadly distributed public-good intervention rather than a supporter-only benefit. IDs: `5B.8`, `5B.6`.
- [Indonesia Growth and Jobs Report: Running Faster, for Longer](https://www.worldbank.org/en/country/indonesia/publication/indonesia-growth-and-jobs-report-running-faster-for-longer-structural-transformation-productivity-and-good-jobs) — World Bank — 2024 — The report says growth delivered jobs and poverty reduction over time, but that Indonesia still needed reforms to deepen broad-based productivity gains. IDs: `5B.8`, `5B.6`.

**Negative**
- [Analysis: A decade of Jokowi, Indonesia’s democracy icon, leaves illiberal legacy, critics say](https://theprint.in/world/analysis-a-decade-of-jokowi-indonesias-democracy-icon-leaves-illiberal-legacy-critics-say/2310394/) — Reuters via ThePrint — 2024-10-14 — Reuters’ end-of-term framing emphasizes patronage, dynastic politics, and weaker institutional integrity, which is the main sign that gains were not allocated purely on public-interest grounds. IDs: `5B.8`, `5B.5`.
- [Jokowi seeks Golkar takeover to retain decade-long influence](https://www.thejakartapost.com/indonesia/2024/03/20/jokowi-seeks-golkar-takeover-to-retain-decade-long-influence) — Reuters via The Jakarta Post — 2024-03-20 — Reuters reported efforts to install a loyal ally in Golkar and preserve influence after office, a direct patronage signal rather than neutral distribution. IDs: `5B.8`, `5B.5`.
- [Protests across Indonesia as parliament delays change to election law](https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/indonesia-shelves-plan-revise-election-law-protests-rage-2024-08-22/) — Reuters — 2024-08-22 — The proposed rule changes were widely seen as benefiting Jokowi’s youngest son and consolidating family advantage, which is a strong anti-fairness signal. IDs: `5B.8`, `5B.5`, `4B.2`.
- [Indonesia leader accused of bias, interference in presidential election](https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/indonesia-leader-accused-of-bias-interference-in-presidential-election-2024-02-01/) — Reuters — 2024-02-01 — Perceived non-neutrality and visible alignment with Prabowo show how incumbent political power was used to shape the successor field, not to distribute gains impartially. IDs: `5B.8`, `5B.5`, `4B.2`.
- [Indonesia: racism, discrimination against Indigenous Papuans](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/18/indonesia-racism-discrimination-against-indigenous-papuans) — Human Rights Watch — 2024-09-18 — HRW describes longstanding discrimination plus security-force abuse against Indigenous Papuans, which is strong evidence that gains and protection were not being shared fairly with a major regional/minority group. IDs: `5B.8`, `5B.5`.
- [Indonesia’s climate ambitions gain boost through World Bank-supported land administration and spatial planning reform](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/09/30/indonesia-s-climate-ambitions-gain-boost-through-world-bank-supported-land-administration-and-spatial-planning-reform) — World Bank — 2024-09-30 — The same reform evidence also shows the need to correct land disputes and unequal tenure security, implying prior distribution remained uneven. IDs: `5B.8`, `5B.6`.
- [OECD Economic Surveys: Indonesia 2024](https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/oecd-economic-surveys-indonesia-2024_de87555a-en/full-report/accelerating-growth-and-attaining-socioeconomic-convergence_02e70f46.html) — OECD — 2024-11-26 — OECD says Indonesia still had price controls, procurement hurdles, high administrative burdens, FDI restrictions, and weak SOE governance, which tends to favor incumbents over broad-based competition. IDs: `5B.8`, `5B.4`, `5B.5`.
- [World Bank Group debars PT LPPSLH Konsultan](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/07/10/world-bank-group-debars-pt-lppslh-konsultan) — World Bank — 2024-07-10 — The bank cited overbilling and the improper hiring of a project official’s family member, a concrete favoritism signal inside a development project. IDs: `5B.8`, `5B.5`, `5B.6`.

**Search Gap**
- Direct 2024 evidence on **class-by-class or region-by-region fiscal incidence** is limited. The best available evidence is indirect: poverty/health/infrastructure gains on the positive side, and patronage, Papua discrimination, and incumbent-protecting regulation on the negative side.
- I did not find strong 2024 evidence that Jokowi explicitly used economic transfers to reward supporters in a direct, programmatic way; the stronger negative case is **structural favoritism and unequal access**, not a documented handout scheme.
